app.name: Founder-Friendly Task Board
app.purpose: Help a solo founder turn product ideas into a small prioritized work queue without losing the reason each task matters.

workflows.goal: Capture a product task, record why it matters, and place it in a visible priority order.
successCriteria: A task keeps its user problem and intended outcome beside its priority.
Changing priority does not erase the original task intent.

responsibilityBoundaries.responsibility: Preserve task purpose and priority rules outside purely visual page rendering.

relationships: A task belongs to one local project list.

data.backupRecovery: Not applicable because this example intentionally proves only in-memory prototype behavior.
data.syncConflictPolicy: Not applicable because this example has no synchronized or shared data copies.

errorAndEmptyStates: The empty queue explains how to add the first task.
A task without a purpose is rejected with useful feedback.
performanceRisks: A future large task list may require filtering or virtualization; this prototype makes no large-data claim.
securityPrivacyRisks: The example uses no accounts, secrets, external AI calls, or durable personal data.

unit.reason: Priority and required-purpose rules need unit tests when the example becomes executable.

integration.reason: The module fixture validates the complete example contract and its evidence links.

ui.reason: No executable UI is claimed by this documentation-only example.

migration.reason: The example has no durable storage or historical schema.

regression.reason: The module test keeps the example structurally valid and reference-complete.

manualQa.reason: Human usability review remains open because the example is not a runnable product.

unresolvedAcceptance: Executable UI behavior and human usability remain deliberately unclaimed.

constraints: Keep this artifact clearly labeled as an example rather than real application acceptance.
nonGoals: No account system, collaboration, durable storage, deployment, beta, or release claim.
openQuestions: Which runtime and storage model should be selected if this example becomes a real application?
